claims.notes: [BATCH NOTE b098] Batch b098 covers lines 1-183 of results/evaluation-scopes.md only; a sibling batch (b099) covers lines 184-369. Scope decisions for this batch, per instrument rule 5: dates and timestamps (2026-08-02, 2026-04-16, 2026-05-03, 2026-04-24), git commit hashes (`6d804934`, `90890ae9..c6023034`), session numbers (Session 78, Session 82), erratum identifiers (E41, E72), hypothesis identifiers (H1-H12, H8 v2 etc.), phase identifiers (Phase 1, Phase 2b, Phase 3a), section references (§3, §4, §5.3, §9, §10, §11, §12), CRS codes (UTM Zone 35N, EPSG:32635), map-sheet names (K-35-052-4 etc.), pool names (pool_020/040/080/160), condition names (`scale-4..8`, `Scale-16/32`, `flash-high-text-16-of-30--flash-min-vf`) and numbers appearing inside file paths (`tiles_384`, `bounds/384`, `h10-384`, `calibration_bounds_160.geojson`) are OUT of scope and were not extracted. SCOPE-COUNT CARE: this document is about tile-set scopes, so 340/487/327/240/160/20 recur as both labels and asserted facts. Applying rule 5's "the 487-tile Era 2 corpus IS a claim" test, every instance where the number is asserted as the size of a set (including inside table cells such as "Era 1 (340 × 512)" and files-manifest descriptions such as "Era 2 bounds (487 tiles, 384 px)") IS extracted; the identical digits appearing only inside a path or a pool name are not. Borderline calls flagged individually below: the §2/§6/§9 table cells and the §5.x heading parentheticals were included on the "asserted fact" side; buffer radii used purely to say which row a metric belongs to ("@ 50 m", "@ 20 m") were treated as row labels, not claims, following the house style of 078.json. The document's own §10 states that no dedicated nesting-check script exists at HEAD, so every area, per-scope GT-mound count, nesting percentage and coverage fraction is recorded as `recompute-script` against the bounds GeoJSONs rather than `read`. One further scope decision, recorded explicitly rather than left silent: the bare adjectival phrase 'zero-tolerance' used as the NAME of the nesting check (lines 10 and 136) is treated as a method descriptor and not extracted, whereas the assertions that quantify it — 'zero area outside the parent', '0.00 sq m outside', 'zero GT mounds are unique to a smaller scope', 'zero overlap' — ARE extracted as values.
